extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural grade-school science questions (multiple choice, non-diagram) partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions), along with the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
extraction.citeAs: Clark et al., 2018. Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected from standardized tests through several months of extensive search and investigation. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science, with queries automatically constructed by instantiating 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Document analysis, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science questions drawn from standardized tests (grade 3-9); web documents retrieved via a major search engine using science-topic queries; the AristoMini corpus (dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences from the Web).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether both an IR solver and a PMI solver answered them incorrectly. The ARC Corpus documents were de-duplicated, stripped to text, and chunked into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the Challenge Set, questions answered incorrectly by both the IR solver and the PMI solver were selected. For the ARC Corpus, web documents were collected, de-duplicated, stripped to plain text, and chunked into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were authored by human examiners for standardized tests and assigned grade levels (3rd through 9th grade) by those examiners. Knowledge and reasoning types were categorized by the authors based on a sample of 100 questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is acknowledged as approximate and subjective: 'These sizes are necessarily approximate, as it requires a subjective judgement about the main challenge exhibited by different questions.'
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (used by the IR solver for filtering Challenge questions); Open IE (used in DGEM-OpenIE baseline)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A leaderboard is maintained for up-to-date results. The dataset, corpus, and models are publicly available at http://data.allenai.org/arc.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The Challenge Set definition using IR and PMI filters may introduce bias: scores on the Challenge Set are near zero for those solvers by design, and the retrieval bias of underlying IR methods is towards sentences similar to the question rather than those that partially match but together explain the answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition only approximates the informal goal of 'hard' questions. The ARC Corpus, while covering ~95% of Challenge questions, cannot be fully exploited by simple retrieval methods. The dataset contains only non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions from grades 3-9.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of question answering systems; benchmarking advanced AI reasoning; the dataset is split into train, dev, and test partitions for the Challenge and Easy sets.
